newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Euro shares higher, dollar below highs.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Euro shares higher, dollar below highs.

text.p: European shares advanced in morning trading on Monday, taking their cue from a rebound on Wall Street, but nagging doubts over interest rates and the U.S. market's outlook helped trim their gains.
"It's been very disappointing this morning. One would have expected a better start to what is effectively the first trading day of the new year," one senior London dealer said.
"People are wary about the interest rate picture. If rates do go up because of rising economic activity, stocks will head south (lower)."
On the bullion market, gold, which has been shunned by investors as stock markets hit record levels in recent months, slipped further to its lowest fixing since October 7, 1993.
The gold price dropped late last week as New York-based investment funds sold. "We've seen continued fund selling last week," one bullion dealer said. "No one wants to touch it."

The dollar, meanwhile, was knocked off its strongest level against the yen since March 1993 after Vice Finance Minister Tadashi Ogawa said Japan would "continue to deal appropriately" with extreme currency market movements.
Excessive weakness or strength in the yen were not good for the Japanese economy, he said.
The dollar, which flirted with 117 yen in Asian trading, had settled around 116.50 in European business before hitting a low of 115.65 after Ogawa's comments -- below late rates last week.
"Japanese officials will get increasingly edgy about seeing yen weakness and I think official disapproval of such a move will be enough to limit it," said Standard Chartered's Tim Fox.
But analysts said negative perceptions of the Japanese economy and low interest rates there still prompted concern over an outflow of funds and should continue to bolster the dollar.
Tokyo markets made a shaky start to the new year on Monday as the yen slid to its lowest level against the dollar in almost four years, dragging stocks and bonds down in its wake.
The 225-share Nikkei average fell by as much as 150 points before reviving to close at 19,446.00, up 84.65 points.
Against the mark, the U.S. currency slipped from a high in Asian trading of 1.5714 but, at around 1.5660 marks, it was still up from Friday's late European levels.

On the London stock market, Europe's busiest, shares started firmer after Wall Street's surge on Friday but fear of higher U.S. and British interest rates was preying on market sentiment and helping to keep trading volumes light.

The Dow Jones industrial average jumped 101.60 points to 6,544.09 on Friday, almost recovering all its losses earlier last week. Analysts said the turnaround suggested investors had shaken off the impact of strong economic indicators -- possible omens of higher interest rates -- on the bond market.

U.S. shares trading in London were slightly higher on Monday. "We were surprised," said one dealer. "The U.S. market is too high by every yardstick but, having said that, today's opening still looks around 10 points higher."
This week the main focus for markets seeking to gauge the temperature of the world's biggest economy will be U.S. jobs figures on Friday.
If non-farm payroll statistics turn out to be stronger than forecast, jitters over higher rates could send markets lower on both sides of the Atlantic, dealers said.
"After the Dow's 100-point jump last Friday, a mark-up in London was inevitable but some players are worried about the Dow's volatility," another London dealer said.
"The market knows the Dow could just as easily drop 100 points in a day, especially if we get any data which hints at higher rates.
"This market has been supported by a low inflation scenario. It does not want to hear the job market is really picking up because more jobs usually means higher wages."
In Frankfurt, which like London was not far from record levels, shares were firmer, aided by the stronger dollar -- good news for German exporters -- and the rebound in New York.
French shares also began the week higher, buoyed by Wall Street's gains and the dollar's performance against European currencies.
CURRENCIES AT 1200 GMT
The dollar was quoted around 1.5660 marks and 115.80 yen, compared with 1.5580 and 116.33 in late business on Friday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1200 GMT
The FTSE 100 index of key British shares was up 14.0 points to 4,103.5.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt was 26.88 higher at 2,886.16. In Paris, the CAC-40 index gained 19.20 to 2,301.96.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $359.25 an ounce in the morning, the lowest since October 7, 1993, and down from Friday's London close of $362.15. Silver slipped two cents to $4.67.
